title: Integrator rapid runway checklist & 90-minute runbook
content:
Context and intent:
This is a working checklist + minute-by-minute runbook for an integrator engineer (internal or customer SDK integrator) to get a minimal Redwood integration live in ~90 minutes. Focus is on high-confidence steps, observable handoffs, and the smallest useful artifacts: sample app, auth, telemetry, and one fallback path.

Audience:
- Platform integrators and SDK partners
- Developer advocates running live demos
- Internal engineers helping customers (Solutions Eng)

Goals (MVP):
1) Get a sample request hitting Redwood in <30 minutes (auth + env).
2) Attach minimal telemetry and a token-level cost view in 60 minutes.
3) Implement a simple fallback to a cheaper model/region and smoke-test in 90 minutes.

Constraints and assumptions:
- Customer has a Redwood account + API key. If not, section A covers quick signup flow with free credits.
- Using a small sample app (Node/Python) that uses our SDK or plain HTTP.
- Network constrained environments: include local-mode instructions.

Runbook (timeboxes):
00:00–10:00 — Prep & creds
- Confirm account exists; locate API key in Console -> API Keys.
- Create a dedicated integration key (label: integrator-temp-<initials>).
- Check region preference: us-west1 or eu-central1.
- Ensure local environment has curl, python3/node14, git installed.
- TODO: add short script to mint short-lived key for demos (security ask).

10:00–30:00 — Hello world request (smoke test)
- Quick options: curl or Python requests.
- CURL example: curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-small-v1","input":"Summarize: company mission"}'
- Python sample (requests):
  import os, requests
  r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', headers={'Authorization': f"Bearer {os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY')}", 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}, json={"model":"redwood-small-v1","input":"Hello world"})
  print(r.json())
- Verify HTTP 200 and sensible JSON. If 401 -> check key scope/expired. If 403 -> org-level ACLs.

30:00–45:00 — Exchange sample into SDK flow
- Install our lightweight SDK (npm i @redwood/inference or pip install redwood-inference).
- Replace raw HTTP with SDK call; show streaming vs non-streaming quick toggle.
- Sample Node snippet:
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference')
  const client = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY})
  const resp = await client.generate({model: 'redwood-small-v1', input: 'Reverse me: abc'})
  console.log(resp.text)
- Note: prefer environment variable auth for demo safety.

45:00–60:00 — Telemetry & minimal observability
- Hook SDK telemetry: set REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=true and point to a project id (instructions below).
- If customer has their own Sentry/NewRelic, show how to forward request_id header to their system.
- Quick logs to add: request_id, model, token_count, latency_ms, error_code.
- Script to emit a small CSV summary for cost review.
- Validation: confirm request appears in Console -> Requests -> filter by apiKey label.

60:00–75:00 — Fallback policy & canary toggle
- Add a simple retry/fallback wrapper in-app:
  1) Try primary model (redwood-small-v1) with 200ms timeout.
  2) On timeout/503/overloaded response, fallback to redwood-tiny-v1 or alternate region.
- Sample pseudo-code for fallback: tryPrimary(); catch (e) { log('fallback', e); callFallback(); }
- Show how to configure route-level fallback in Console (quick demonstration) and how SDK respects route hints.

75:00–90:00 — Smoke tests & gating
- Run 10 sample requests; assert: all 200, average latency < target, fallback exercised once.
- Check Console traces for token counts; estimate per-1000 cost using the quick calc.
- Create a small PR in customer repo with README/ENV instructions and a changelog entry.

Appendix A — Quick signup & API key steps (for completely new accounts)
- Sign up -> verify org -> Billing -> apply free credits -> Create key (Settings -> API Keys).
- Tip: use a namespaced key and remove after demo.

Appendix B — Environment variables & local-mode config
- REDWOOD_KEY=sk-xxxx
- REDWOOD_REGION=us-west1
- REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_PROJECT=team-demo
- LOCAL_MODE=true (uses SDK hermetic runner to simulate responses; useful when offline)

Appendix C — Common pitfalls and remediation
- 401 Unauthorized: key missing/rotated. Remedy: check env and console key scope.
- Rate limit 429: burst throttling — add exponential backoff and batching.
- Strange hallucinations: ensure prompt includes system instructions + temperature. Use model redwood-rlf to reduce.
- High cost: enable token caps, use cheaper model family for non-critical requests.

Appendix D — Minimal test checklist (to include in PR)
- [ ] README with env vars and run commands
- [ ] Sanity test script (10 requests, asserts status==200)
- [ ] Telemetry shows request ids and token counts
- [ ] Fallback path exercised in CI (simulated outage)
- [ ] Cost estimate documented in cents per 1k tokens

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Can we produce a tiny CLI that automates the 90-minute flow? (CLI: redwood-onramp init)
- Need a short-lived demo key API for internal advocates — security consult needed.
- Add a one-click Console template that prepopulates a route + fallback policy and demo key.
- Decide default fallback priority: cheaper model vs region vs serverless vs dedicated.

Useful links & references:
- Integrator Onramp Hub (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEV/Integrator+Onramp+Hub
- Sample repos: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples (node/python)
- Telemetry design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Telemetry+Design

Change log (working):
- 2024-08-15 Priya K: created initial flow and timeboxes.
- 2024-08-20 Diego M: added fallback pseudo-code and telemetry checklist.
- 2024-09-01 Ava C: updated CLI idea, added quick signup appendix.

Notes for finalizing (next pass):
- Turn this into a small 'onramp' guide in docs.redwood.ai with runnable examples and CI tests.
- Produce a short slide deck (5 slides) for Solutions Eng to drive workshop sessions.
- Convert smoke tests into a tiny action that runs on PR to validate integration.

(Informal/fragments below — keep while drafting)
- Quick snippet for token-cost calc: cost = tokens * model_rate_per_token; round up per-call.
- Want a tiny demo that shows streaming vs non-streaming side-by-side.
- Potential to add a preflight.js that verifies envs and echos downstream services.

End of document.
